text:
rob: Heads up — after the CUDA 12.2.1 driver roll on prod-gpu pool we are seeing ~18-25% throughput regression for small-seq (<=64) chat workloads. Perf graphs show higher p99 and lower tokens/sec.

anya: :eyes: which kernel is regressing? any autotuner logs?

rob: Profiling points to the attention matmul kernel selection. The autotuner is choosing the fallback generic GEMM path for sm86/90 on short sequences instead of the tuned fused attention kernel. Here is a small snippet from the sampling run: 

```
[profiler] candidate kernels: fused_attn_sm86 (est=1.2ms), generic_gemm (est=0.9ms)
[autotune] picked: generic_gemm (measured=1.8ms)
[notes] measured > est by x2. heuristics mismatch after driver update
```

kevin: Interesting — so estimates are stale vs measured. Could be changed kernel performance after driver/CUDA libcudnn micro-optimizations. Did we update any kernel availability checks?

rob: We double-checked kernel availability. The binary selection still exposes fused_attn_sm86 but its measured latency jumped on driver 12.2.1 nodes. Looks like the driver changed warp scheduling or math path. Autotuner cost model didn't adapt because it reuses cached timing histograms keyed by (arch, seq_bucket, batch). The cache still contains pre-upgrade timings.

sanjay: Can we invalidate the autotune cache for the pool and let it re-probe? Quick mitigation would be to force the old kernel choice while we investigate.

rob: Agreed. Two mitigation options tested locally: 
1) Force kernel override via env: REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=fused_attn_sm86
2) Disable online autotune: REDWOOD_AUTOTUNE=0 (fall back to static policy)

I ran a canary with REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=fused_attn_sm86 on 3 nodes — tokens/sec recovered to pre-roll numbers, p99 back to expected.

deployer: infra-bot shows the driver roll was performed at 1750000900 by image-promote pipeline. No other infra changes.

infra-bot: deploy: promoted image gpu-runtime:v2025-03-13-driver12.2.1 to prod-gpu-pool at 1750000900.

anya: What's the risk of forcing kernel? Could expose correctness issues or slower perf at other seq lengths.

rob: Risk is low for fused_attn on short seqs — correctness unchanged. For longer seqs the runtime still chooses other paths. We limited override to seq_len<=128 via the per-route config: 

```
route.config.kernel_override {
  seq_max: 128
  kernel: fused_attn_sm86
}
```

kevin: Rollback strategies: 
- Fast rollback: pin node image back to gpu-runtime:v2025-03-09-driver12.1.8 for prod-gpu pool (full rollback).
- Gradual rollback: patch autotuner to invalidate caches + trigger rebench on a background worker (safe but takes hours).
- Middle ground: force kernel override for affected seq bucket + schedule node image rollback in the off-peak window (02:00 UTC).

sanjay: For auditing, capture pre/post nsight traces and the autotune histograms. Add regression alert to the console: if tokens/sec drop >10% for 5m on any route, auto-suspend autotune and notify #oncall.

rob: Commands I used for canary override: 
```
# set per-route override via admin api
curl -X POST $ADMIN/api/v1/routes/override -d '{"route":"/chat","seq_max":128,"kernel":"fused_attn_sm86"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# or set node env (temporary)
kubectl set env ds/gpu-runtime REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=fused_attn_sm86 -n redwood-prod
```

kevin: Plan decided in triage: 1) Apply seq-bucket kernel override to affected routes now (rolling canary 5 nodes). 2) If metrics recover in 15m, schedule image rollback to 12.1.8 at 02:00 UTC (low traffic). 3) Meanwhile, infra team will add autotune cache invalidation + remeasurement job for the pool. 4) Postmortem to follow.

rob: I patched the override and started the canary at 1750001280. Metrics look good at +22% tokens/sec on canary. Will monitor until 1750001560.

anya: Please dump autotune cache and upload to S3 for postmortem. Also add exact nsys traces to the ticket.

rob: Will do. Uploaded artifact: s3://redwood-perf/1750001234/canary-nsys-trace.zip

kevin: Thanks all. After rollback we should add a driver-compat test matrix to CI: run short-seq perf probes on new driver images before promotion. Avoid surprises like this.

sanjay: +1. Also adding a small autotune fuzz test that compares estimated vs measured latencies and alerts if factor >1.5.

rob: Closing loop here — I'll post a short postmortem draft once we confirm image rollback outcome.

deployer: scheduled image rollback job created: rollback-job-1750001400 (will run 02:00 UTC if green signal). :white_check_mark:
